segments.text: Lie down flat on your back in shavasana. Allow your entire body to become completely still.
State your heartfelt intention or Sankalpa silently three times.
Become aware of your natural breathing. Inhale for four, exhale slowly for seven.
Each prolonged exhale invites deeper surrender into the ground.
Rotate your awareness systematically through the right side of the body: hand, arm, shoulder, waist, leg, foot.
Now the left side of the body: hand, arm, shoulder, waist, leg, foot.
The back of the body: heels, calves, buttocks, spine, shoulder blades, back of the head.
The front of the body: crown, forehead, eyebrows, eyes, throat, chest, navel.
Now count your breaths backwards from 27 down to 1. Inhale 27, exhale 27. Inhale 26, exhale 26.
If you lose count, begin again gently from 27.
Awaken the sensation of intense heaviness throughout the entire body.
Now evoke lightness. Feel as weightless as a feather floating above the ground.
Now warmth... and now soothing coolness.
Visualize a calm, clear lake in early morning. Smooth as glass.
Now an ember glowing gently in a dark hearth, steady and peaceful.
Recall your Sankalpa once more. State it three times with feeling and certainty.
Slowly begin to deepen your breath. Feel the contact points of your body with the floor.
Gently move your fingers and toes. Roll to your right side when you are ready.
Slowly open your eyes. The practice of Yoga Nidra is now complete.
Remain completely relaxed. Let go of all effort. Rest and sleep.
